headline: AI's real limits: permissions, proofs and procurement rules
paragraphs: Anthropic's public formal-math repository now hosts a Lean formalization claiming that VP ≠ VNP over every field — a separation of two algebraic complexity classes that are analogues of P and NP. Two things matter about how this arrived. First, it is a claim in a proof assistant, which means it can be machine-checked, but the posting is not a peer-reviewed validation, so what exists today is an inspectable artifact rather than a confirmed theorem. Second, the material does not explain any AI method behind the proof; Anthropic is hosting it, and the story does not say the company produced or vetted the argument. The claim is also narrower than P vs NP, and it is aimed explicitly at complexity theorists and formal-verification researchers, not at general readers. That combination — a striking mathematical assertion, published openly, shielded from hype by its own incompleteness — sets up the pattern running through the rest of today's stories: capability is arriving faster than the permission layers built around it.

For consumer AI, the binding constraint this week is not model quality but access. Google's AI Mode in Search can now ground answers in a user's Google Drive files and Wallet items, and TechCrunch reported on November 23 that the same Personal Intelligence capability is being extended to the standalone Gemini app. Note the shape of it: the personalization runs inside Google's existing ecosystem rather than through a third-party connector, and the report did not say which countries or account types get it, whether users must opt in, or which Drive data is in scope. ByteDance is hitting the mirror-image problem. GeekPark argues that Doubao has reached an ecosystem wall — it can book a Caocao ride but cannot tap send on a WeChat message, because WeChat, Taobao and Meituan are among more than 150 apps on Doubao's October 14 list that bar the assistant from operating their pages. The only Doubao phones on sale come from ZTE's Nubia, the M153 engineering sample at 3,499 yuan and the NaviX Ultra at 5,999 yuan, and GeekPark says about 200,000 units are planned for 2026 against 57.9 million smartphones shipped in China in the third quarter. An assistant that owns its ecosystem can borrow your files; an assistant that does not gets stopped at the send button.

A second thread is the return of building the stack yourself, and with it a candid admission of what is unfinished. Ladybird released its first alpha on November 23, 2026, installable on macOS and Linux without compiling; the engine implements its own HTML parsing, CSS, layout, JavaScript and WebAssembly, borrowing externally only for text shaping (HarfBuzz), 2D graphics (Skia), video (ffmpeg) and SQLite, with separate processes per tab. The project warns that some sites will not work and makes "no promises about security today," inviting security researchers to attack it. Myriota, the Australia-based satellite IoT firm, raised roughly $40 million in a first close of its Series C, per the Wall Street Journal's Rhiannon Hoyle; its sensors connect directly to Myriota's own satellites rather than to terrestrial networks, and the company said the money goes to hiring and to scaling the constellation. The report gives no investor names, no valuation and no total target, so the round is unconfirmed as complete. In both cases the strategic logic is vertical: own the layer beneath, accept that the first version is visibly imperfect, and let outsiders do the checking.

Energy and grid policy supplied the quieter but more consequential moves. Jordan's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources said at the inaugural Jordan-EU Investment Conference that it will invite private investors early next year to build a 200 MW solar plant and a 100 MW/400 MWh battery storage system on a build-own-operate model, with the state-owned National Electric Power Company buying the solar output and acting as beneficiary of the storage project; the ministry puts solar investment at roughly $100 million to $130 million, with a prequalification request expected in February 2027. Saudi Arabia's Electricity Regulatory Authority replaced a 2 MW ceiling on renewable self-consumption with a 50 MW cap and explicitly permits integrated battery storage, pv magazine reported, citing a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency; the rules cover solar, wind, waste-to-energy and biofuel, split grid-connected systems into four bands from 1–11 kW up to 50 MW, and require no prior approval or connection payment for systems up to 11 kW. Both countries are shifting from state-built to privately financed capacity, and both now treat batteries as standard equipment rather than an exception.

The open questions are concrete. The Lean posting has no named author in the account given, no peer review, and no explanation of how AI figured in producing it — anyone citing it as an Anthropic result is ahead of the evidence. Google has disclosed the capability but not the opt-in terms, geography or data scope, which are exactly the details that determine whether "personal intelligence" is a feature or a default. GeekPark's 200,000-unit figure for Doubao phones is a projection, not a shipment number, and the wall it describes is commercial, not technical — it breaks when app makers decide it does. Watch the Lean artifact for review by complexity theorists; watch whether Google publishes opt-in and rollout specifics; watch whether Doubao's blocked-app list shrinks; watch Ladybird for its first external security findings; and watch Jordan's February 2027 prequalification to see whether the build-own-operate model actually draws private capital.
takeaways: Anthropic's repo hosts a Lean claim that VP ≠ VNP over every field, but it is unreviewed and the posting describes no AI method behind it.
Google can personalize AI Mode with Drive and Wallet data inside its own ecosystem, while ByteDance's Doubao is blocked by more than 150 apps from acting on theirs.
Jordan and Saudi Arabia both moved this week to let private developers build solar and battery capacity under clearer, higher caps.
